maya: pushed a quick patch to the kernel selector that prefers int8 matmul on A100 for Qwen-3 small when batch_size<=8. seeing a weird regression though :confused:
fergus: ugh, can you paste the perf numbers?
maya: baseline (fp16) -> p50 42ms, throughput 280 tok/s. after selector change -> p50 48ms, throughput 240 tok/s. spike on long context (>2k tokens) only.
jia: did you run with kv cache warmup enabled? that often hides the first-pass cost.
maya: yes, warmup enabled. profiler shows a new kernel fallback happening at step ~10: `matmul_int8_fallback` then we go to `matmul_fp16` for remainder.
sam: that fallback smells like calibration mismatch. which quant profile did it pick?
maya: selector picked `qwen-3_small_int8_profile_v3` from /models/quant-profiles/ but v3 was tuned on short seqs.
natalie: could be the scale factors saturating with longer seq lengths, forcing a different kernel path. any logs?
maya: pasted snippet:
```
[2026-11-12 10:12:34] kernel_selector: chosen int8_matmul (config id qwen-3_small_int8_v3)
[2026-11-12 10:12:34] matmul_int8: calibration stats mean_scale=0.12, max_scale=1.8
[2026-11-12 10:12:34] matmul_int8: overflow_detected -> falling back to matmul_fp16
```
fergus: that max_scale=1.8 is high for the quant table we expected. Maybe quant calib used a different activation distribution.
jia: did the batch composition change? mixing very long and very short requests can blow up max activation if we don't clamp.
maya: yes we started a canary with mixed_batching heuristic that groups by arrival not by seq len. trying to emulate production.
sam: mixed_batching is more efficient at throughput but you need prefix clipping or per-sample clamping pre-quant. otherwise int8 tables get noisy.
natalie: propose two immediate actions: 1) revert kernel selector to prefer fp16 for seq>1024, 2) run new calibration with long-seq samples and publish as v4 profile.
fergus: +1. Also add a runtime guard: if overflow_count > 0.5% in first 20 steps, fallback permanently for that worker and emit metric.
maya: i'll open a tiny PR for the selector revert and guard. also uploading the failing trace to s3: s3://redwood-ml/triage/qwen-int8-longseq-1795129876.tar.gz
jia: for calibration, we should sample from production prompt sets (chat+code+system). I can prepare a 2k-token corpus for re-calib.
sam: FYI switching to fp8 kernels might avoid some of this, but we don't have production-grade fp8 matmul on the line yet. fp8 likely better dynamic range but different numeric shape.
natalie: can we share the new profile to the team? prefer a git-backed canonical location so deploys can pin by commit.
maya: plan: create models/quant-profiles/qwen-3_small/int8/v4/{profile.json,meta.txt} and a short README with known-good workloads. i'll also add a `recommended_runtime_hint` field that the runtime can read.
fergus: also add a `batching_compat` tag: e.g. "compat": ["length-aware-batching"] so the selector only chooses the profile when the batcher guarantees grouping by seq len.
sam: nice. for telemetry, add metrics: `quant_overflow_rate`, `kernel_fallback_rate`, `selected_profile_id` with sample labels. then we can graph regressions quickly.
jia: quick experiment idea: run replay of the failing trace with per-layer clipping at 6*sigma (empirical) and see if fallback disappears. cheap to test locally.
maya: doing that now, will post results.
eng-ml-bot: deployment notice: canary build 2026.11.12-1795 deployed to dev cluster (maya) :rocket:
maya: update: per-layer clipping removed fallback, p50 back to 43ms, throughput ~275 tok/s. so the issue is activation tails in long-context mixing.
natalie: conclusion: mixing heuristic needs an override or profiles must declare safety constraints. we should standardize profile metadata and a small linting tool to validate a profile against workload samples.
fergus: i'll prototype a validator that runs quick simulated activations and checks overflow risk. put it in infra/quant-tools/validator.py.
sam: sounds good. can we put the v4 profile into the shared `quant-profiles` bucket AND create a short note in #eng-ml/docs? ops wants the rollout checklist.
maya: uploaded v4 and opened PR to runtime to read `recommended_runtime_hint` and `batching_compat`. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/447 :eyes:
jia: thanks — once the validator is in, run it on v4 and add the validation badge to the profile meta.
maya: will do. marking this thread for follow-up: revert landed (1795130123), v4 uploaded (1795130300), validator PR incoming.
natalie: :thumbsup: great triage. we'll schedule a 15-min sync tomorrow to formalize profile metadata fields and batching contracts.
fergus: adding an action: update runbooks with guidance: "if kernel fallback occurs, check selected_profile_id -> if profile batching_compat incompatible, revert selector and re-calibrate".
maya: noted. closing thread once validator PR is merged.
